source.place: Trace-transport setup specialized to the constant coefficient object; hidden construction in the rationality proof's Step 4

proof.text: Use the normalized constant datum of [lem-zl-constant-weil-datum], not an arbitrary Weil structure on the underlying constant sheaf. Its geometric and model Weil maps send each constant stalk element $a\in A_n$ to $a$. For $m\geq1$, the iterate in [def-trf-iterated-weil-map] still sends $a$ to $a$: the base case is the specified map; adjoining the next pulled-back map composes the identity with the identity on the constant stalk. The pullback-composition identifications merely regroup these same constant coefficient identifications. The same calculation applies to the geometric iterate in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. In particular no scalar multiplier or Tate twist is introduced by iteration.

source.place: Setup, normalized compatible tower and its rationalization; expansion of the constant-datum specialization

proof.text: Fix a closed point $y$ and a point $x\in Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^{d_y}})$ above it as in the statement. In the local geometric construction of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], follow a constant coefficient $a$ through the point transport of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport]: restriction takes the constant section $a$ to the constant section $a$, insertion into the inverse-image colimit keeps its label $a$, and the pullback comparison sends it to $a\otimes1$. The canonical constant structure from [def-weil-constant-weil-structure] sends $a\otimes1$ back to $a$. Repeating this $d_y$ times and applying Step 1 gives $F_y=1$. This computation is valid at each finite level and on the completed coefficient object: there the canonical structure is defined by its commuting projections to the finite levels, so the same calculation fixes every compatible family $(a_n)_n$. At the rational stage both the point transport and the constant structure are their integral maps tensored with $E$, hence fix every $a\otimes\lambda$. The stalk is $E$ in degree zero by the rational constant datum [lem-zl-constant-weil-datum]; there are no other cohomological degrees. The return used here is $g_Y^{d_y}\bar x=\bar xg_s^{d_y}$, not an equality $g_Y^{d_y}\bar x=\bar x$.

source.place: Setup, rationalized constant datum; explicit geometric local transport on constant sections

proof.text: At finite level use instead the displayed local composite in [def-trf-frobenius-operators], with $m=d_y$. Its first arrow $\rho_{x,m}$ identifies the constant stalk with the stalk pulled back by $\Phi^m$ at the fixed point, and keeps $a\in A_n$ unchanged. The remaining arrows compose as $\varphi_n^{[m]}\circ\kappa^{(m)}$, exactly the scheme-Frobenius map $u_m$ of [def-trf-iterated-weil-map]. For $m=1$ this is the canonical model map by the last sentence of [lem-zl-constant-weil-datum]. By the multiplicative-iterate assertion of [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison], for successive $m$ this composite is the composite of the pulled-back canonical model maps, all identities on constant stalks by Step 1. Thus the complete composite sends $a$ to $a$, and $F_{x,d_y}=1_{A_n}$ for every $n$. The transitions are coefficient reductions, so these identities are compatible and induce the identity on the integral realization. Rationalizing that identity gives $1_E$ on the rationalized constant datum. This uses realization of the whole compatible system followed by rationalization; it does not tensor an individual torsion module $A_n$ with $E$.

source.place: Setup, compatible finite-level Weil pairs; explicit constant model-map stalk calculation

proof.text: For either rational local operator obtained in Steps 2 and 3, choose the single-element basis $(1)$ of the one-dimensional $E$-vector space $E$. The matrix of $1-T^{d_y}F_y$ is the $1\times1$ matrix $(1-T^{d_y})$. Its determinant, by the one-term determinant formula, is $1-T^{d_y}$. The constant complex is concentrated in degree zero, so the alternating stalk determinant has just this factor. Its formal inverse is $\sum_{j\geq0}T^{jd_y}$, since multiplying by $1-T^{d_y}$ cancels every coefficient of positive degree and leaves constant coefficient $1$.

source.place: Clause (b), local determinant specialized to the constant rank-one stalk

proof.text: Apply [prop-euler-product] to the finite-type scheme $Y_0$. It gives the coefficientwise locally finite identity $Z(Y_0,T)=\prod_y(1-T^{d_y})^{-1}$ over $\mathbf Q$. Its notation is that of [def-weil-point-counts-zeta], which agrees here with [sk-def-zeta]: both use the same field-valued points over the specified subfield $\mathbf F_{q^r}\subset k$, and both define $Z=\exp(\sum_{r\geq1}N_rT^r/r)$ and $d_y=[\kappa(y):k_0]$. The finite-type finiteness of these point sets supplied by clause 1 of [lem-weil-point-counts-finite] means that the infinite-set convention in [sk-def-zeta] never intervenes. Thus this is exactly the zeta series occurring in the conclusion, not a series of unnormalized point counts.

source.place: Closed-point and integral-series identity, displayed product and its local finiteness

proof.text: Fix $M\geq0$. Clause 2 of [lem-weil-point-counts-finite] makes the set of closed points with $d_y\leq M$ finite, and by [prop-euler-product] only these points affect the product modulo $T^{M+1}$. Each other local factor from Step 4 is $1$ modulo $T^{M+1}$. Apply the coefficientwise ring homomorphism $\iota:\mathbf Q[[T]]\to E[[T]]$ of [def-weil-coefficientwise-ring-hom-map] to this finite truncated product. It preserves multiplication and fixes $T$ and $1$, hence sends each inverse factor to the inverse of $1-T^{d_y}$ (apply it to the equation defining the inverse). It follows that modulo $T^{M+1}$ the product of the constant-sheaf local determinant inverses is $\iota Z(Y_0,T)$. The same finite set of factors works over $E$, proving local finiteness there. Taking $M$ equal to each coefficient index proves equality of the formal series. For $M=0$ all products have value $1$ modulo $T$; if $Y_0$ is empty every product is the empty product $1$.

title: Constant sheaf local factors and zeta L-series
statement: Fix the finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$ and $E=\Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. Let $Y_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] with $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, equipped with the normalized compatible constant datum of [lem-zl-constant-weil-datum]. For every closed point $y$ of $Y_0$, of degree $d_y=[\kappa(y):k_0]$, the one-circuit local Frobenius on the constant stalk $E$ in degree zero is the identity in both of its forms: the operator $F_y$ of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] for the canonical Weil structure $(E_Y,\theta_E)$, and the operator on $E$ obtained by integral realization of the compatible stalk operators $F_{x,d_y}$ and then rationalization of [def-trf-frobenius-operators] for the levels $((A_n)_Y,\varphi_n)$ of that datum, where $x\in Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^{d_y}})$ is a point with image $y$ (given by a $k_0$-embedding $\kappa(y)\hookrightarrow\mathbf F_{q^{d_y}}$); each finite-level operator $F_{x,d_y}$ is the identity of the stalk $A_n$. Hence, for either operator, the local determinant factor is $\det(1-T^{d_y}F_y\mid E)=1-T^{d_y}$. The Euler product defining the constant sheaf's $L$-series, namely $\prod_y\det(1-T^{d_y}F_y\mid E)^{-1}$, is coefficientwise locally finite and equals the coefficientwise image of $Z(Y_0,T)$ [sk-def-zeta] under $\iota:\Q\hookrightarrow E$ [def-weil-coefficientwise-ring-hom-map].
